title: A tilted block with a dry east side
text: The Sierra Nevada is a huge block of the earth's crust that has been sharply uplifted and exposed on the east along the Sierra Nevada fault system and tilted westward. Rocks west of the Sierra fault moved up to create the modern mountains, while those to the east moved down to form a valley. The range forms a barrier to storms from the Pacific and creates a rain shadow east of the crest. The shallow western slope has pine forests and alpine lakes, while the steep eastern slope is barren and dry.
